summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against all seven paragraphs of the selected Greek. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Both preserve the conditional liability for believing slander, repeated liability, universal giving, recipient judgment contrast and explicit negation, giver innocence, unqualified life promise, and personal and household repentance. The disclosed service-to-God attachment remains a permissible working reading; the alternative life-to-God attachment is retained in the notes. The notes distinguish the heart conjecture and bracketed possessive from preserved wording, and distinguish reported corrections and reconstructions from manuscript readings. Their principal witness disclosures agree with the supplied bounded project reports. Acceptance concerns fidelity to this working source and consistency of disclosure, not authentication of unseen editions, manuscript images, correction hands, or exhaustive collation.
